correctness.rationale: For nonzero m-dimensional complex Lie algebra g, C(g)={(x,y):[x,y]=0} is bihomogeneous. The C* action [x:y] -> [tx:y] preserves bracket-zero equation. A fixed projective point with x,y both nonzero would require its rescaling factor equal both t and 1, impossible for t!=1. Both coordinate P(g) subspaces are fixed and lie in C(g) since [x,0]=0. Hence fixed locus is disjoint P^{m-1} plus P^{m-1}, Euler localization yields chi_top(P C(g))=2m=chi(P^{2m-1}); both-nonzero open has chi_c=0. No reductivity or normality premise. Independent bilinearity checks on nonabelian 2D bracket verify formal identity; result is analytic algebraic C* localization, not finite extrapolation.

value.rationale: The commuting variety is canonical for representation and Lie theory and has complicated singularities even in reductive cases. An exact invariant for its projectivization for every (even nonreductive) finite-dimensional complex Lie algebra, with topological cancellation on both-nonzero commuting pairs, is a naturally reusable classification. The computation is short and applies general fixed-point technology, but the universal all-Lie-algebra statement is not a random unmotivated slice or mere dimension restatement.
